doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Red Caillou and his move to California
summary: Pasley describes his boyhood friend Red Caillou, who moved to California about 1925 and died in Oakland.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: He was in New Orleans. Yeah, you know, you know Red Caillou? Yeah. Yeah, piano player. Yeah? Yeah.

Oh, we good friends. Oh, do you know his real name? No, I think he's, no, all I know is Red Caillou. Now, I know he's got some cousins and some uncles. I don't know if he named that today or not. He got a, he got a uncle named George. What did he play? They didn't play no music. Oh. Oh, yeah. No, I didn't play no music. I know Red Caillou, he died up here in Oakland.

Do you know when? About 18 years ago. 18 years ago? Mm-hmm. About 18 and 19 years ago. You met him still here in California? No, I know him in New Orleans when I was in short pants. He was older than you? About one year. Oh, only one year. Yeah. Oh, my God, I know him a long time. Somebody told me his real name was Joseph Caillou. Could that be?

Could be, but all I know, we call him, everybody called him Red Caillou. Yeah. That's, you know. He was a light fella? Yeah. Yeah. Real light fella. Did he have a- Short. Little short. Yeah.
